body.heading: Actions have partners
paragraphs: Almost every action has an opposite — an action that undoes it or faces the other way. Open undoes close. Push is the partner of pull. Learning actions in pairs makes both words easier to remember.
Read each pair, then act it out. Your hands will learn the words before your head does!

body.heading: Open and close, push and pull
paragraphs: Open — She opens the gate. Close — He closes the gate.
Push — He pushes the cart. Pull — She pulls the wagon.

body.heading: Up and down, on and off
paragraphs: Up — The kite goes up. Down — The kite comes down.
Turn on — He turns on the lamp. Turn off — She turns off the lamp.

body.heading: Fill and empty, give and take
paragraphs: Fill — He fills the cup. Empty — She empties the cup.
Give — She gives the book. Take — He takes the book.
Fold — He folds the towel. Unfold — She unfolds the towel.
Laugh — She laughs. Cry — He cries. (Feelings have opposites too!)

body.heading: Think and talk
paragraphs: 1. Play opposites charades: one person acts an action, the other must act and say its OPPOSITE.
2. Which pair do you use most at home — open/close, on/off, or give/take?

takeaway: Opposite actions come in pairs — open/close, push/pull, fill/empty, give/take — and each one helps you remember the other.
